 Micho ahead of Union Berlin clash: “We’ll be ready!” 
 Go to the comments section Add to your bookmarks Share this article Following the international break, the Red Bulls travel to 1. FC Union Berlin on Saturday (15:30 CET) . Another win would see Leipzig continue their fine run of form and strengthen their position among the Bundesliga’s leading sides. RBL head coach Martín Demichelis spoke to the media ahead of the trip to Berlin. Who’s available for selection? What kind of opposition is Micho expecting? And what does he make of our attacking firepower?
 On the international break and the fitness of the returning players
 “ None of the players who were away on international duty have come back with injuries , which is good news. However, Nici, Banzu, Abdoul, Baumi and Toni didn’t train with us today. Tomorrow will be our first session with the full squad. 
 OneFootball Videos
 I’m pleased that everyone has come back fit and that things went well for them all. We now need to focus on the next run of fixtures. We’ve got eight games in less than a month and a chance to make some real progress.”
 On Brajan Gruda ’s development and his Germany debut
 “I’m really pleased for him and, of course, for RB Leipzig too. Developing players is one of our objectives as a club. He had two fantastic games, scoring some lovely goals and providing assists. He still needs to keep his feet on the ground and continue working hard.
 It’s always special to play for your country, but then it’s important to perform for your club again. The next challenge for him is the game against Union, where he’ll need to show once again just how good he is.” 
 On Union Berlin
 “We’re in for an intense atmosphere. I’ve never been there before, but I’ve heard all about it. They’re a tough side to face, but we’ll have our fans there to support us too. We’ll be ready! 
 We’ve made some good progress in recent games and need to carry a lot of that into Saturday’s match . We need to be brave and play our football right from the off.”
 On our goalscoring form and unpredictability in attack
 “ I’m really pleased about that. We said from the outset that we wanted to be a team that’s difficult to play against while playing attractive football. At the same time, we still need to become more solid.
 Having several players who are capable of scoring goals is a big advantage, but it doesn’t matter who scores. What matters is getting the three points.”
 On possibly rotating the squad ahead of the Champions League
 “Union Berlin are our priority right now. It would be a huge mistake to go into the game against Union with one eye on Tuesday. We’ll field our strongest line-up on Saturday. After that, our focus will switch to Lens.”
